note: Minimal state-service file: two one-line accessors (IsInCombat/IsMoving) reading SkuCore fields, plus namespace setup and doc comment. No duplication, dead code, naming/style inconsistency, redundant work, or localization ternaries present.

Clean file. 143 lines, all functions are reachable public Sku API, no dead code, no duplication, consistent t-/a- naming, single build loop with no hoistable repeated work. The one German string (line 54) is a plain literal, not a GetLocale deDE ternary, so no localization finding applies.

findings.summary: The two CreateTextBox setter callbacks in MacroMenuBuilderNew are byte-identical except for the target field, each doing the same C_Timer.After(0.1) OnSelect+OnUpdate re-pin.
findings.suggestion: Factor the shared body into a small local helper, e.g. `local function setField(field, value) aParent[field] = value; C_Timer.After(0.1, function() SkuOptions.currentMenuPosition:OnSelect(); SkuOptions.currentMenuPosition:OnUpdate() end) end`, and call it from both CreateTextBox setters. Purely structural; the runtime sequence (set field, then re-pin next frame) is unchanged.
findings.gain: Removes a near-identical re-pin block that a future edit to the post-set menu re-pin logic would have to change in two places, avoiding a desync where only one of the two form fields gets updated.

findings.summary: GetMacroInfo(i) is destructured into name, iconTexture, body, isLocal but only `name` is ever used; iconTexture/body/isLocal are unused locals.
findings.suggestion: Reduce to `local name = GetMacroInfo(i)`.
findings.gain: Removes three unused locals that falsely imply the icon/body/isLocal values are consumed here, so a future reader/edit does not mistakenly rely on them being populated.

findings.summary: MODULE_NAME is declared but never used anywhere in the file.
findings.detail: MODULE_NAME is only referenced at its declaration (line 23). The one place that needs the parent addon name, line 26 (LibStub NewAddon fallback), uses the string literal "SkuCore" directly instead of MODULE_NAME. Only MODULE_PART is actually used (NewModule/RegisterToggleableModule). So MODULE_NAME is a dead upvalue.
findings.suggestion: Drop MODULE_NAME from the declaration: `local MODULE_PART = "AudioDevice"`. Leave line 26's literal as-is (or, if desired for consistency, this is the sole consumer — but simplest is to just remove the unused name).
findings.gain: Removes a dead upvalue and the false implication that the SkuCore literal on line 26 is kept in sync with MODULE_NAME; a future edit changing MODULE_NAME would silently not affect line 26.

findings.summary: Inline GetLocale()=="deDE" label ternary for the feature's display name.
findings.detail: The toggleable-module label is produced by the inline `(GetLocale and GetLocale() == "deDE") and "Audiogerät" or "Audio device"` pattern rather than going through the Sku.L localization table used for every other spoken/displayed string in this file. Single occurrence (the aggregate localization item the review brief allows).
findings.suggestion: Route the label through Sku.L like the rest of the file's strings (behavior-preserving if the L entries resolve to the same two strings).
findings.gain: Consolidates the one label that bypasses Sku.L into the same localization path as the rest of the file, so a future language change has a single source of truth instead of an inline exception.

findings.summary: Header comment claims output goes through print(), but tSay uses DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage.
findings.detail: Lines 18-20 state "All output goes through print() so SkuChat's screen-reader pipeline speaks it automatically." The actual implementation (tSay, lines 46-48) routes through DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage, not print(). Stale/inaccurate comment describing the output routing.
findings.suggestion: Update the comment to reference DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage to match tSay.
findings.gain: Prevents a future edit that trusts the header (e.g. changing print() behavior) from touching the wrong output path; the comment currently misdescribes the screen-reader routing mechanism.

findings.summary: ua/ub are computed with a truncated single-value expression on line 890 and then immediately recomputed correctly on line 891, calling tSkuFollowProbePos(tUnit) twice.
findings.detail: Line 890 `local ua, ub = tUnit and tSkuFollowProbePos(tUnit) or nil, nil` assigns ua = only the FIRST return of tSkuFollowProbePos (truncated, non-final position) and ub = nil, then line 891 `if tUnit then ua, ub = tSkuFollowProbePos(tUnit) end` re-calls the same function and assigns both. When tUnit is set the position API is invoked twice and the line-890 value of ua is dead; when tUnit is nil line 890 correctly yields nil,nil. The line reads like a bug (looks like it intends to get both coords but only gets one).
findings.suggestion: Replace line 890 with `local ua, ub = nil, nil` and keep line 891 as the sole assignment. Identical observable result, one fewer API call, and the confusing truncated expression is gone.
findings.gain: Removes a redundant UnitPosition call per probe run and eliminates a line that looks like a latent coord-truncation bug a future edit could copy or 'fix' wrongly.

findings.summary: `local f = _G["SkuPerformance"] or CreateFrame(...)` sits inside `if not _G["SkuPerformance"]`, so the `_G["SkuPerformance"] or` fallback is always nil and never taken.
findings.detail: The enclosing guard at line 446 is `if not _G["SkuPerformance"] then`, so inside that block `_G["SkuPerformance"]` is guaranteed nil and the `or` short-circuit always evaluates CreateFrame. The `_G["SkuPerformance"] or` prefix is dead.
findings.suggestion: Simplify to `local f = CreateFrame("Frame", "SkuPerformance", UIParent, BackdropTemplateMixin and "BackdropTemplate")`.
findings.gain: Removes a dead sub-expression so the create-vs-reuse branching reads unambiguously; this is the sighted-only perf frame (no audio/menu/voice path).

findings.summary: Two large commented-out C_Engraving mock blocks (GetEngravingModeEnabled/IsEngravingEnabled overrides and GetRuneCategories/GetRunesForCategory stub data plus SetCVar/LoadAddOn) sit at the top of the file.
findings.detail: These are commented-out SoD engraving experiment stubs kept as reference. They are inert but add ~50 lines of clutter at the very top of the addon-bootstrap file and reference hardcoded rune IDs that will rot over time.
findings.suggestion: Delete the two commented blocks (git history preserves them) if they are no longer an active reference.
findings.gain: Removes ~50 lines of stale commented mock data from the first-loaded file; marked low/low since it is deliberate reference code and may be intentionally retained.

findings.location: SellJunkFunc, line 68 (table established once at line 55)
findings.summary: The custom-junk-id set is re-resolved via SkuSettings:Sub() on every bag slot of every ticker pass instead of being hoisted once.
findings.detail: SellJunkFunc ensures SkuSettings:Sub("SkuCore", nil, "char").SellJunkCustomItemIds exists at line 55, then at line 68 re-invokes the full :Sub("SkuCore", nil, "char").SellJunkCustomItemIds[itemID] chain inside the nested bag(0-4) x slot loop. The table is never reassigned during the scan, so the repeated :Sub() method call plus multi-level table walk is pure recomputation on a 0.2s ticker across all bag slots.
findings.suggestion: After line 55, capture `local customIds = SkuSettings:Sub("SkuCore", nil, "char").SellJunkCustomItemIds` and read `customIds[itemID]` at line 68. Identical result since the table reference is fixed for the duration of the call.
findings.gain: Eliminates one :Sub() call plus a 3-level table traversal per occupied bag slot per 0.2s ticker iteration; the value is provably invariant within the call.

findings.summary: Local tSouldSomething is written but never read, so it is dead and misleadingly implies it gates something.

findings.suggestion: Remove the tSouldSomething declaration and its assignment.
findings.gain: Removes a write-only variable that a future editor could mistake for a live 'did we sell anything' flag and wire into logic incorrectly.

findings.summary: escapes and escapesChat are hand-maintained near-duplicate pattern tables that have already silently desynced.
findings.detail: escapesChat is meant to be escapes minus the raid-target-icon pattern (per the comment at lines 20-21 and the commented-out line 35). But it is ALSO missing the ["|A.-|a"] atlas-texture pattern that escapes has at line 27. Nothing documents that omission as intentional — only the {.-} raid-icon difference is called out. This is exactly the desync duplication invites: the two tables share 4 identical entries maintained by copy-paste, so any future pattern added to escapes must be remembered in escapesChat too. The consequence today is that Unescape(str, aChatSpecific=true) does not strip |A...|a atlas markup, so such markup would leak into chat/voice output.
findings.suggestion: Derive escapesChat from a single source of truth (e.g. build it from escapes and delete only the ["{.-}"] key) so the shared patterns cannot diverge. NOTE: doing so would start stripping |A in the chat path, which CHANGES behavior (voice/chat output), so it must not be applied blindly as a pure cleanup — first confirm whether the missing |A is an intended exception or a bug, then either add |A to escapesChat (bug fix) or add an explicit comment documenting the omission (like the {.-} one) to prevent future 'fixes'.
findings.gain: Removes a real copy-paste desync between two pattern tables (escapesChat already lost the |A pattern) and surfaces a latent output bug where atlas markup is not stripped from chat/voice text; prevents future pattern edits from silently applying to only one path.

findings.location: tIsGem, lines 77-113 (GetItemInfoInstant path 81-96 vs GetItemInfo path 102-113)

findings.suggestion: Extract the shared checks into one local helper, e.g. tClassifyGem(itemType, itemSubType, itemEquipLoc, classID, subClassID) returning boolean, and call it from both paths (unpacking each API's return values first). Purely a code move; the same conditions run in the same order.
findings.gain: Removes a real double-maintenance hazard: any future tweak to the gem heuristic (a new classID, another localized substring) must currently be applied in two identical blocks; missing one silently desyncs Instant-path vs cache-path gem detection, which changes which bag items appear in the socket menu.

findings.location: num-slots block in tCollectBagGems (lines 182-186) and tBagSlotFrame (lines 305-309)

findings.location: lines 170-171 comment above tUsedGemSlots ("Wird bei AcceptSockets, Abbrechen oder Fenster-Schliessen zurueckgesetzt.")

findings.summary: tBody is read from GetMacroBody but never used; the function is an effective stub whose success message overstates what it does.
findings.detail: `local tBody = GetMacroBody(tIdx) or ""` assigns a value that is never referenced. The following tSay claims the macro was 'geloggt. /skulog export.' but nothing is actually logged (no dprint/log call). The read result is discarded.
findings.suggestion: Remove the unused `local tBody = GetMacroBody(tIdx) or ""` assignment (behavior-preserving). The misleading 'geloggt' message would need a real dprint to actually log, but that changes voice/log output so is out of scope for a behavior-preserving cleanup.
findings.gain: Removes a dead read of the macro body and flags a diagnostic that silently does nothing despite reporting success, preventing a future reader from trusting the 'logged' claim.

findings.summary: Loop index variable tBookType is unused and misleadingly named (it is the numeric index 1/2, not the book type).
findings.detail: `for tBookType, tType in ipairs({ "spell", "pet" })` binds the numeric index to tBookType, but the body only ever uses tType (the actual 'spell'/'pet' string, also stored as bookType). The index is never read, and the name suggests it holds the book type it does not.
findings.suggestion: Replace tBookType with _ (or drop it): `for _, tType in ipairs({ "spell", "pet" })`. Behavior is identical.
findings.gain: Eliminates a misnamed unused loop variable that a future edit could grab expecting the string 'spell'/'pet' and instead get 1/2, a real value-confusion bug risk in the spellbook scan.

findings.summary: The 'count entries in tLog.unique via pairs' idiom is duplicated verbatim in two functions.
findings.detail: Both tAppend (`for _ in pairs(tLog.unique) do tCount = tCount + 1 end` to test against MAX_UNIQUE) and tDumpSummary (same loop to print the unique count) hand-roll an identical size-of-hash-table count. There is no shared helper, so the two sites can drift if the unique store's shape or counting rule ever changes.
findings.suggestion: Extract a file-local `local function tUniqueCount(tLog) local n=0 for _ in pairs(tLog.unique) do n=n+1 end return n end` and call it from both sites. Pure refactor, identical result.
findings.gain: Removes a duplicated count loop so a future change to how unique entries are counted (e.g. tracking a live counter) only has to be made once instead of being silently missed in one of the two call sites.

findings.summary: tNow() (a date() call) is invoked twice to set firstSeen and lastSeen on a freshly created unique entry.
findings.detail: On the new-entry path both `firstSeen = tNow()` and `lastSeen = tNow()` call date() separately. Beyond the redundant syscall, the two strings are intended to be equal for a brand-new entry but can differ by one second if the calls straddle a second boundary.
findings.suggestion: Compute `local tTs = tNow()` once above the table literal and assign both `firstSeen = tTs` and `lastSeen = tTs`.
findings.gain: Saves one date() call per newly-seen fingerprint and guarantees firstSeen==lastSeen for a new entry, removing a latent one-second inconsistency at second boundaries.

findings.summary: The SkuDebugLog lazy-init guard `if type(SkuDebugLog) ~= "table" then SkuDebugLog = {} end` is copy-pasted verbatim in all three job-completion callbacks.
findings.suggestion: Optionally hoist the guard into a tiny file-local helper (e.g. `SkuDBToolsEnsureLog()`) and call it from each tDone. Purely a de-duplication; the runtime effect is byte-for-byte identical.
findings.gain: Removes a three-way desync risk: a future change to how the persisted store is initialized (e.g. adding a version field or a different table shape) currently has to be edited in three separate places, and missing one would silently diverge the three logs.

findings.location: RangeCheckUpdateRanges default-config literal, lines 72-151 (Friendly = lines 81-115, Hostile = lines 116-150)

findings.summary: SkuSettings:Sub("SkuCore", nil, "char") is re-invoked up to 5x per DoRangeCheck call on a value that does not change within the call.

findings.location: DialTargetingRosterUpdate, raid block lines 251-271, raid10 block lines 275-296, party block lines 302-336
findings.summary: The three group branches repeat the same 10x5 attribute-clear loop, roster-fill loop, and NUMPADPLUS/NUMPADDECIMAL bindings almost verbatim.

If the eligibility rule ever changes and only one copy is updated, RosterUpdate and EndableDisable would disagree about whether the feature is active, producing bindings that target a roster that was never populated.

findings.summary: Four of the six dispatcher handlers dprint the literal 'DialTargeting_PARTY_LEADER_CHANGED' regardless of which event actually fired.

findings.summary: UpdateTradeAcceptBinding re-implements the exact SkuKeyBinds store-read that the tKeyBindKeys helper already provides.
findings.detail: tKeyBindKeys(aConst) walks SkuOptions.db.profile["SkuOptions"].SkuKeyBinds and returns (key, key2) with "" fallbacks. Lines 749-753 inline that identical walk for "SKU_KEY_TRADEACCEPT" (tKb chain, then tEntry.key / tEntry.key2 with "" fallbacks) instead of calling the helper. Every other keybind read in this file (nav, USE, right-click, plus tBindBagKey/tBindCharKey via GetBindingKey) funnels through a single accessor; this is the lone inline copy of the SkuKeyBinds path.

findings.gain: Removes a second hardcoded copy of the SkuOptions.db.profile.SkuOptions.SkuKeyBinds path; if that store location ever moves (as W1's SkuSettings migration work has been reshaping), the inline copy would silently keep reading the old path and break trade-accept binding while the helper-based reads still worked.

findings.summary: The 3-line "reset currentMenuPosition to menu root" block is copied verbatim four times inside the kroute handler.
findings.detail: All four sites are byte-identical: `if SkuOptions.Menu and SkuOptions.Menu[1] then SkuOptions.currentMenuPosition = SkuOptions.Menu[1] end`. This reset is load-bearing (the index lists it as an invariant at lines 448-456 / 531-540: without it CheckFrames' restore-across-rebuild branch re-navigates to a stale position). Four copies of a correctness-critical reset are four places a future fix must be kept in lockstep.
findings.suggestion: Hoist a file-local helper, e.g. `local function tResetMenuToRoot() if SkuOptions.Menu and SkuOptions.Menu[1] then SkuOptions.currentMenuPosition = SkuOptions.Menu[1] end end`, and call it at the four sites. Same code executes, same order relative to the surrounding SkuClearBagPostAction/CheckFrames calls.
findings.gain: Collapses four copies of a correctness-critical menu-cursor reset into one, so a future change to the root-reset semantics can't be applied to three sites and missed on the fourth (which would leave a stale currentMenuPosition on the missed path).

findings.summary: The cooldown branch gates on the CrowdControlled mute setting but plays the Cooldown sound — the mute key does not match the sound it guards.
findings.detail: Line 166 tests `SkuSettings:Sub("SkuCore").UIErrors.CrowdControlled ~= tOff` but line 167 plays `...UIErrors.Cooldown`. Every other branch tests the same key it plays. findings.summary: The exact expression sqrt((sx-dx)^2 + (sy-dy)^2) is computed twice on the same return line — once wrapped in floor() and once bare.

Distance is a hot nav helper (distance-to-waypoint/target). Hoisting to a single local and returning floor(local), local is byte-for-byte equivalent output.
findings.suggestion: local d = sqrt((sx - dx) ^ 2 + (sy - dy) ^ 2); return floor(d), d
findings.gain: Halves the per-call arithmetic (one sqrt + two pow + two subtractions saved) on a frequently-called distance helper; identical return values.

findings.gain: Removes a desync risk: a future edit to the bearing math currently has to be made in two spots to keep clock-direction and compass-word announcements consistent.

findings.suggestion: Extract a single helper, e.g. `local function tEnsure(aKey) local p = SkuOptions and SkuOptions.db and SkuOptions.db.char and SkuSettings:Sub("SkuAuras", nil, "char"); if not p then return nil end; p[aKey] = p[aKey] or {}; return p[aKey] end`, and define `tEnsureSets`/`tEnsurePending` as thin wrappers (or call `tEnsure("Sets")`/`tEnsure("PendingSets")` directly). Behavior is identical.
findings.gain: Removes a duplicated guard chain that must currently be kept in sync in two places; a future change to the nil-guard or the Sub scope (e.g. adding a safety check) can no longer be applied to only one copy and silently diverge.

findings.summary: SkuSettings:Sub("SkuAuras", nil, "char") is called a second time right after tEnsureSets/tEnsurePending already resolved the same char sub-table.
findings.detail: In SetsCreateFromAllAuras, `tEnsureSets()` (line 71) already computes `SkuSettings:Sub("SkuAuras", nil, "char")`, then line 73 recomputes the same Sub call just to read `.Auras`. Same pattern in AcceptPendingSet line 132 after `tEnsurePending()` at line 130. The two calls return the same table, so the second lookup is redundant.
findings.suggestion: Have the ensure-helper (or a small shared accessor) return the parent char table alongside the target list, or read `.Auras` from the already-resolved parent, so Sub is resolved once per call.
findings.gain: Eliminates one duplicate table-resolution lookup per snapshot/accept action; also removes the latent risk of the second Sub call being nil-unsafe (line 73/132 index `.Auras` on the Sub result without the guard the ensure helpers apply).

findings.summary: The timeStamp select-value previews are off by one: index [3] reuses SkuChat.timeStampFormats[2] (same as index [2]), so from index [3] on every preview label is formatted with the wrong format and timeStampFormats[7] is never previewed at all.
findings.detail: values[2]=Format 1 uses formats[2] (HHMM); values[3]=Format 2 ALSO uses formats[2] (HHMM) — should be formats[3]; values[4]=Format 3 uses formats[3]; values[5]=formats[4]; values[6]=formats[5]; values[7]=formats[6]. Because the stored value (1-7) is what Core applies via timeStampFormats[value], selecting e.g. index 3 shows a HHMM preview but Core actually applies HHMMSS (formats[3]); formats[7] (HHMMSS_24HR) can be selected but its preview shows a HHMM_24HR string. findings.suggestion: Align each values[n] preview with SkuChat.timeStampFormats[n] (values[3] should use formats[3], values[4]=formats[4], ... values[7]=formats[7]). Do NOT change silently — this alters displayed menu/voice labels, so it needs an explicit go-ahead.
findings.gain: Fixes a latent display bug where the timestamp preview shown/spoken for indices 3-7 does not match the format Core will actually apply, and where one format is unreachable in the preview.

findings.location: soundSettings group leaves — the `set = function(info,val) ... end` blocks at lines 186-193, 210-217, 234-241, 258-265, 282-289

findings.location: SkuQuest:GetTTSText — tText (declared line 530, ~20 assignments through 734), tGold/tSilver/tCopper (591-594), tTextObjectives (532)

findings.summary: CheckQuestProgress(PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD_flag) is called twice back-to-back with identical arguments.

findings.summary: Two uncalled functions: GetQuestTitlesList has no caller anywhere in the repo (grep shows only its definition), and OnQuestLog_OnEvent is an empty stub whose only reference is a commented-out hooksecurefunc on line 1167.

findings.summary: SplitStringBTTS and SplitString are near-identical gsub pipelines differing only in which punctuation substitutions are active and the final space handling.

This is the same copy-paste-then-diverge pattern that TokenizeNumberToAudio (#19) already unified via an aMode parameter, so a mode-parameterised single function is feasible.
findings.suggestion: Consider unifying into one function taking a mode flag (mirroring TokenizeNumberToAudio's aMode) so the shared substitution list lives once; only if the divergence can be encoded exactly. Given this is voice-output text, verify by-ear before merging.
findings.gain: Two ~50-line copies of the tokenizer stay in sync only by hand today; unifying prevents a future substitution-table edit from being applied to one path and not the other.

findings.summary: The off-hand weapon-enchant reporting block is unreachable dead code because it tests undefined variables hasOffHandEnchantID / hasOffHandExpiration instead of the names GetWeaponEnchantInfo actually returns (offHandEnchantID / offHandExpiration).
findings.detail: Line 843 destructures GetWeaponEnchantInfo() into ...hasOffHandEnchant, offHandExpiration, offHandCharges, offHandEnchantID. The block then guards on `if hasOffHandEnchant == true then` (valid) but immediately does `if hasOffHandEnchantID and hasOffHandEnchantID > 0 and SkuDB.WotLK.enchantIDs[hasOffHandEnchantID]` — hasOffHandEnchantID is a nil global, so the inner branch is never entered and tName is never built. hasOffHandExpiration (line 919) is likewise nil. The main-hand block just above (844-897) uses the correct mainHandEnchantID/mainHandExpiration, so it works; only the off-hand path is broken by the typo. Net effect: off-hand weapon enchants are silently never announced in the Shift-Up overview.
findings.suggestion: Behavior-preserving cleanup: delete the unreachable inner block. The load-bearing fix (rename hasOffHandEnchantID->offHandEnchantID and hasOffHandExpiration->offHandExpiration to actually report off-hand enchants) CHANGES runtime behavior, so treat that as a bug fix, not a silent cleanup — flag it to the maintainer to decide.
findings.gain: Removes ~50 lines of provably unreachable code, and surfaces a real user-facing bug: off-hand weapon enchants (e.g. oils/poisons) are never spoken in the overview reader for a blind user.
